finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts::read-only note viewers now open a yorkie `doc.update()` on every remote change
evidence: The mechanical part of the claim is accurate: note-sync.ts:56-61 calls `this.store.batch(...)` for every docChanged ViewUpdate before the `Transaction.remote` filter, and YorkieNoteStore.batch (yorkie-note-store.ts, `batch`) unconditionally opens `this.doc.update((root, presence) => ...)`, so a read-only viewer applying a peer edit does enter `doc.update`. But the inferred harm does not follow: `Document.update` in @yorkie-js/sdk only commits, queues a local change, touches the undo stack and publishes events inside an `if (context.hasChange())` guard, so an empty body produces no change, no `localChanges` entry, and therefore no PushPull/auth-webhook traffic — `doc.update` is purely local and never itself hits the server or the permission path that `ensureText()` avoids (ensureText actually writes `r.content`). The PR's own integration test 'applies a peer edit without recording a local undo unit' exercises precisely this remote-only ViewUpdate path against the real SDK and asserts the undo stack is unchanged, which would fail if the empty update registered anything. I could not read node_modules here (empty worktree), so confidence is medium rather than high, but the residual cost is a no-op context allocation per remote transaction, not a correctness or permission defect.
